passage: Supervisor's note, Friday. Observed: Pradeep, junior technician, spent last month shadowing Bindu on the repair bench. Bindu gave up several lunch hours to walk Pradeep through fault-finding. Today Pradeep handed Bindu a handwritten card and said, in front of the whole bench, "You taught me to trace the fault before touching the board. I want to do that for the new apprentice." Bindu looked embarrassed and pleased and said it was nothing. Pradeep has already run one short session with the apprentice this week, using Bindu's checklist, and asked me whether the studio could spare both of them an hour on Fridays. What I did: agreed to the hour and told Bindu what Pradeep had said. 🙂 Chaitanya

qa.q: What did Pradeep hand to Bindu?
qa.a: Pradeep handed Bindu a handwritten card.

qa.q: What did Bindu's embarrassed and pleased look suggest?
qa.a: Bindu was touched by the thanks but modest about it, saying it was nothing.

qa.q: What step did the supervisor take to support the mentoring?
qa.a: The supervisor agreed to an hour on Fridays for Pradeep and the apprentice, and told Bindu what Pradeep had said.

qa.q: How might the new apprentice benefit from Pradeep's plan?
qa.a: The apprentice gets short sessions using Bindu's checklist, so what Bindu taught is passed on.

grounding: A supervisor's note shows a junior thanking a mentor sincerely, applying what was taught, and passing it on to an apprentice.
